note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a CRO 8; A06b CRO 8; L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 8 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships (with major exceptions); a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Dual citizenship restriction), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. The coding also records a dual-citizenship restriction on descent, which the form doesn't hold. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primary was read: Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o hrvatskom državljanstvu, Narodne novine 130/2011, čl. 2; Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o hrvatskom državljanstvu, Narodne novine 102/2019 (in force 1 January 2020), čl. 1-2. It confirmed the years of residence, birth in the territory, descent and the limit abroad. It was silent on renunciation and loss on taking another citizenship, which still rest on the sources above, re-read that day and found the same.

sources.said: Person has been resident in Croatia for 8 years immediately before the application. ... Renunciation or automatic loss of another citizenship, unless the person is stateless (a statement is sufficient if the other country does not allow renouncing citizenship, or places conditions which cannot be fulfiled) or is the spouse of a citizen (see A08). ... n.a. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Croatia to a citizen. ... Dual citizenship restriction ... Person is born abroad to two citizens.; Person is born abroad to at least one Croatian citizen and birth is registered in Croatian consulate or registrar (in Croatia) before the age of 21, or person is older than 21 and within two years from the entry into force of the law (i.e. 1 January 2022) person submits application for registration as Croatian citizen (conditional on Interior ministry security checks). Or person is born abroad to a parent who is a citizen and another parent who is stateless or of unknown citizenship. ... No provision ... No provision

sources.title: Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o hrvatskom državljanstvu, Narodne novine 130/2011, čl. 2
sources.said: U članku 8. stavku 1. točka 3. mijenja se i glasi: »3. da živi u Republici Hrvatskoj s prijavljenim boravkom 8 godina neprekidno do podnošenja zahtjeva i ima odobren status stranca na stalnom boravku;«.

sources.title: Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o hrvatskom državljanstvu, Narodne novine 102/2019 (in force 1 January 2020), čl. 1-2
sources.said: članak 4. mijenja se i glasi: »Podrijetlom stječe hrvatsko državljanstvo dijete: 1. čija su oba roditelja u trenutku njegova rođenja hrvatski državljani; 2. čiji je jedan od roditelja u trenutku rođenja djeteta hrvatski državljanin, a dijete je rođeno u Republici Hrvatskoj; ... Osoba rođena u inozemstvu, čiji je jedan roditelj u trenutku njezina rođenja hrvatski državljanin, a ne udovoljava pretpostavci iz stavka 1. ovoga članka, stječe hrvatsko državljanstvo ako bi ostala bez državljanstva.«
